counter_evidence:
I wrote a fresh stress harness in the session scratchpad, at C:\Users\User\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-User-Documents-projects-EMS-workshop1--claude-worktrees-knowledge-store-research-9c609c\f3bbe503-2a20-4258-976b-7d457d3bf63a\scratchpad\kc3r-scripts\master.cjs and worker.cjs. It uses built-in modules only and follows the design's writer exactly: writeFileSync to events/<aa>/<id>.json.tmp-<pid>, then renameSync to events/<aa>/<id>.json, with all processes released by a start barrier. It ran on this box: Node v24.22.1, libuv 1.52.1, NTFS on C:, Windows 11 10.0.26200. Results:

(1) 8 writers x 1,000 identical events: 99 renameSync EPERM (errno -4048, syscall rename) and 99 leftover .tmp files. The final .json count was correct at 1,000 and no file's hash differed from its name.
(2) 8 x 1,000 with half the events shared: 62 EPERM, 62 leftover tmp files, 4,500 correct files.
(3) Proposal D's own case, 4 x 300 identical events, run twice: 17 and 20 EPERM, and the same numbers of leftover tmp files. Proposal D's "0 errors" did not reproduce.
(4) 8 x 1,000 identical events with 2 concurrent readers doing the design's readdir and read freshness scan: 114 EPERM, 114 tmp files left. The readers made 69,476 reads with no torn or mismatched content.
(5) Checking existsSync before writing made it worse: 1,803 EPERM and 1,803 tmp files.
(6) Control with all events unique (8 x 1,000, with and without readers): 0 errors, 0 tmp files, 8,000 correct files. Only replacing an existing destination fails.

A deterministic single-process probe shows the mechanism. A destination held open by any handle, even a libuv fd (libuv opens with FILE_SHARE_DELETE), makes fs.renameSync(tmp, dest) fail with "EPERM rename". The same rename succeeds once the fd is closed. Renaming onto a name that does not exist always succeeds.

So rename-over-existing on NTFS through Node fails whenever another process has the destination open. That process can be a concurrent identical writer, the freshness reader in every CLI call, a git add by the lease holder, or the antivirus. The active AV here is 360 Total Security; Defender's real-time protection is off (Get-MpComputerStatus RTP=False). The fd test shows the failure does not need any AV.

The winning design (docs/program/KNOWLEDGE-STORE-DESIGN-2026-11.md line 218) renames before the BEGIN IMMEDIATE ingest, and every call runs the readdir freshness scan. Writers are therefore not serialised at the rename, and readers overlap it.

A previous scratch run from another session (scratchpad\ks-c3\run1.log) independently recorded 199 to 439 EPERM per 8 x 1,000 identical-event run.
narrowed_claim: n/a. Only part of the claim held in every run: the content of each final file was intact (no file's sha256 differed from its name, no empty files, no torn reads), and unique-name writes never failed. The "no error" and "no leftover temp file" parts are false whenever an identical event is written at the same time or the destination is open.
what_would_settle_it: Already settled by reproduction on this box. To re-run: node master.cjs <dir> 8 1000 same 0 always (in kc3r-scripts) shows the EPERM count and the leftover tmp files. The single-process probe (open dest, then renameSync over it) gives EPERM deterministically.
design_consequence:
LB2/KS-C3 cannot be used as written. KS1's journal writer must never rely on renaming over an existing file. Two variants were tested here (8 x 1,000 identical events plus 2 readers; the verify variant was also run with half the events shared, 8 x 1,000 plus 2 readers), and both gave 0 errors, 0 tmp files, 0 hash mismatches and the correct file count:

- (a) Preferred: no-replace publish. fs.linkSync(tmp, final); on EEXIST, read final and accept it as a dedupe only if its sha256 equals the id; then always unlinkSync(tmp). Result: 1,000 links, 7,000 dedupes.
- (b) Rename, and on EPERM/EACCES/EBUSY verify final's hash, then unlink tmp. If final is absent or wrong, retry with bounded backoff. Result: 95 dedupes.

Also:
- A tmp file that cannot be cleaned up must never be journaled: put `*.tmp-*` in the store's .gitignore, keep the freshness scan reading only names ending in `.json`, and have ks doctor sweep or report tmp files whose pid is dead.
- KS1's done-when stress test must include concurrent readers, one destination held open by an fd, and the 4 x 300 case. Its pass criterion is the protocol's output (0 unhandled errors, 0 tmp files after cleanup, hash equals name), not raw renameSync success.
- Proposal D's "4 x 300, 0 errors" must not be cited as evidence.
